messages.subject: Re: Goodness-of-fit tests in oSCR?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nina,

Unfortunately we have not included this capability into oSCR yet.  Goodness-of-fit is a complicated subject and the approaches to quantifying it properly are computationally expensive.  There are some shortcuts available but their robustness is not well understood.  On the to-do list for sure!

On Monday, September 28, 2020 at 5:23:21 PM UTC-4 morrel...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> Apologies if this has already been answered in this group. I'm wondering if there are any tests for goodness of fit that can be used for oSCR models beyond comparing relative AIC values. Something along the lines of the function secr.test in package secr (https://rdrr.io/cran/secr/man/secr.test.html), that might allow me to assess the fit of the model to the underlying data. So far I've been unable to find any resources for calculating test statistics of this nature specifically for oSCR.fit objects.
>
> Thanks in advance!
>
> Nina
>
>

messages.subject: Re: Flexibility in specification of linear model of density?
messages.subject_clean: Flexibility in specification of linear model of density?
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I sent this a while back, and I never got a response which means either a) it's a silly question or b) no, there isn't.  Having dug through the source (a bit) it looks like the answer is no, it isn't possible with oSCR "as is" - is that correct?

Best,
Dan

On Sun, Aug 16, 2020 at 7:50 AM Daniel Barton <croft....@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi All,
>
> I'm wondering if it's possible in oSCR (and if so, how) to specify linear models of density that are more complex than just, for example:
>
> D~cov*session
>
> For instance, what about a model where the interactions are specified by hand - such as when one has missing level combinations (i.e. interaction(factorA, factorB, drop=T).  I can see how to modify some of the source code (i.e. the model.matrix calls in oSCR.fit) to maybe make this happen, but I'm not sure if there is already an implemented approach I'm not catching.  Alternatively, it may be that missing level combinations are handled gracefully by nlm deeper in oSCR but I'm thinking that might not be the case.
>
> THANKS,
> Dan
>
> --
> --
> Dan Barton
>
> Note: this is not my official Humboldt State email.

--
--
Dan Barton

messages.subject: Re: [oscr] Re: Flexibility in specification of linear model of density?
messages.subject_clean: [oscr] Re: Flexibility in specification of linear model of density?
messages.body_plain:
hi Dan,
 I may not fully understand the full scope and complexity of your question but I do think if you can define the covariate explicitly (as an interaction or whatever) then you can just add it as a column to the state-space dataframe  -- so if you have the interaction(factorA, factorB, drop=T) and this implies some number of dummy variables or whatever, then you should be able to add those as columns to the ssDF , say called var1, var2, var3...., varN  and then model D ~ var1 + var2 + ....

 That should work fine, for any variable that you can define explicitly, and without having to rely on general R model specification formula conventions.
regards
andy
